care: Readings are for reflection and guidance. They do not replace medical, legal or financial advice, and the choices stay yours.

readings.title: Readings
readings.line: Psychic and intuitive readings, tarot and oracle cards, and readings on love, work, your path, your ancestors and your gods.
readings.note: Tarot began as a card game in fifteenth-century Italy; it was first used for divination in eighteenth-century France.

seeing.title: Other ways of seeing
seeing.line: Mirror, water and fire scrying, the pendulum, the open book, and quiet guidance on your spiritual path.
seeing.note: Scrying is gazing into a still or reflective surface (a mirror, water, fire) until images come. Bibliomancy is opening a book at random and reading where your eye falls.

dreams.title: Dreams
dreams.line: Understanding your dreams and their symbols, remembering them, protecting your sleep, and asking a dream to come.

eye.title: The inner eye
eye.line: Meditations and workings to grow your intuition, sharpen your discernment and trust what you sense.

astral.title: Between worlds
astral.line: Preparing for astral work, crossing with care, and the rituals of the seasons when the veil is said to be thin.

mirror.label: Press and hold to still the mirror for a prompt to ponder
mirror.idle: Press and hold the mirror, and be still
mirror.hint: A symbol rises with a prompt to sit with: something to ponder, never a prediction. There is no right answer.

prompts.prompt: What are you ready to walk through?
What is already in your hand?
Where is the path asking you to go?
What wants your warmth and attention?
What would you do if you felt free?
What is moving on its own, if you let it?
What is growing in the dark?
Where are your roots?
What have you already noticed, but not yet trusted?
What two things are you being asked to join?
What is small now, and will grow?
What would it mean to let this pass?
What would you see if you held a little more light to it?
What connects the things you keep thinking about?
What is asking for your patience?
What are you making a home for?
What lies deeper than your first answer?
What could grow from the place that felt like mud?
What do you protect, and what does it protect you from?
What would it be like to hold this lightly?
Which way are you leaning, before you decide?
What is quietly burning down, and what is it lighting?
What keeps returning, and what has changed each time?
What still guides you, even from far away?

close.title: Bring a question, or just yourself
close.lede: Tell Sarvakali what you are wondering about. A reading begins there.
